title: Finite equations for a finitely generated affine zero locus
statement: A finitely generated ideal on an affine open has a finite set of generators whose basic opens characterize its zero locus.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Tag 07RZ, proof, second paragraph

proof.text: Unpack Ideal.FG to obtain a finite set t with Ideal.span (t : Set Γ(S, W)) = I. Rewrite the zero locus using this equality and Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zeroLocus_span. Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.mem_zeroLocus_iff and Finset.mem_coe then give precisely the stated finite conjunction. No affine hypothesis or membership in W is needed for this implication.

proof_origin.text: Direct proof from the definition of Ideal.FG and Mathlib Scheme.zeroLocus_span and Scheme.mem_zeroLocus_iff; this implements the finite-generators step of Stacks Tag 07RZ.

mathlib_searches.query: quasi finite flat morphism degree rank locus quasicompact affine open
An affine open fibre degree sublevel locus is cut out by finitely many sections for a flat separated quasi finite finitely presented scheme morphism

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_equations_of_finitely_generated_zeroLocus {S : Scheme.{u}} {W : S.Opens} {I : Ideal Γ(S, W)} (hI : I.FG) : ∃ t : Finset Γ(S, W), ∀ s : S, s ∈ W → (s ∈ S.zeroLocus (U := W) I ↔ ∀ a ∈ t, s ∉ S.basicOpen a)
